children: Shares of regional banking company Valley National Bancorp

jumped 5.1% in the afternoon session after the company reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings per share and revenue above Wall Street expectations. According to the company’s press release, Valley National reported net income of $206.3 million, or 36 cents a diluted share, compared with $170.9 million, or 29 cents, in the prior quarter and $163.4 million, or 28 cents, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings of 36 cents topped the 33-cent consensus, and revenue of $584.15 million topped the $577.83 million consensus. Chief Executive Ira Robbins tied the record quarter to revenue growth and expense discipline that pushed the efficiency ratio to 49.4%, below 50% and the best level since the third quarter of 2021. Net interest margin on a tax-equivalent basis rose 8 basis points to 3.28% as adjustable-rate loans repriced higher and new commercial originations came on at better yields, while customer deposits increased $1.1 billion to $55.2 billion. Management said the bank is on track to finish 2026 at the high end of its guidance ranges and still expects to reach, and likely exceed, a 15% return on average tangible common equity by the end of 2027, from 14.2% this quarter. Pending acquisitions of Providence Financial and Bluevine, both expected to close in early 2027, are meant to add lower-cost deposits. Net charge-offs did rise, to $37.1 million from $22.0 million in the prior quarter.
What is the market telling us

Valley National Bank’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 1 move greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful, although it might not be something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 8 months ago when the stock dropped 6.2% on the news that hotter-than-expected inflation data and rising concerns over credit risk rattled investors. January's Producer Price Index (PPI), a measure of wholesale inflation, rose 0.5% against expectations of 0.3%, with the core component jumping 0.8%. This report fuels the narrative of "sticky inflation," suggesting the Federal Reserve may have limited room to cut interest rates. Compounding these worries are growing anxieties in the credit markets. According to a Bank of America strategist, problem loans are an increasing concern that could pressure lenders. Investors are reassessing credit risk, particularly in private-credit and leveraged-loan markets, weighing on the valuations of banks sensitive to the economic cycle.

Valley National Bank is up 17.2% since the beginning of the year, but at $13.71 per share, it is still trading 9.8% below its 52-week high of $15.19 from July 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Valley National Bank’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $993.12.
